notes: This focused trace covers two bounded missing-parameter paths: omitting the declared HLAsyncPointName from HLArequestSynchronizationPointStatus and supplying zero parameters to HLAsetSwitches, which must receive at least one. Both paths require the standard HLAreportMOMexception with HLAparameterError true and the fully qualified interaction name. The tests do not constrain provider-specific synchronous exception types or HLAexception wording, do not cover every MOM interaction or extra-parameter rejection, and do not claim full Table 20, MOM, or synchronization-point conformance.

requirements.statement: The test invokes the standard sendInteraction service with the standard MOM interaction class and an empty ParameterHandleValueMap.

HLArequestSynchronizationPointStatus declares HLAsyncPointName to identify the synchronization point whose status is requested. HLAreportMOMexception shall be sent when a MOM interaction is sent without all necessary parameters; its HLAservice value identifies the interaction class fully qualified, its inherited HLAfederate identifies the joined federate, and HLAparameterError is HLAtrue for an incorrect number of interaction parameters.

requirements.source_lines: page 291, line 101; standard MIM HLArequestSynchronizationPointStatus parameter declaration
requirements.statement: The TCK sends HLArequestSynchronizationPointStatus without the declared HLAsyncPointName and verifies that the RTI reports the missing required MOM interaction parameter with HLAparameterError true. This is a bounded witness for that interaction only; it does not establish parameter completeness for every MOM interaction or every Table 20 exception.

The TCK sends HLAsetSwitches with zero parameters and verifies that the RTI reports this missing-parameter form through HLAreportMOMexception with HLAparameterError true. This directly witnesses the at-least-one-parameter rule for HLAsetSwitches only.
